CTICU Sim Lab

The cardiac surgery patient in real time, from the operating room to the ICU bedside: run bypass and separation, pace from epicardial wires, run a CALS arrest, read the PA catheter, decide bleeding vs tamponade, wean the vent and troubleshoot the balloon pump, Impella and ECMO.

      Event log

      • Events appear here as they happen.

      Bedside reference

      Failure to capture
      Spike, no P/QRS after it, no pulse. Raise output, check cable, reverse polarity, pads on.
      No spike when expected
      Open circuit or oversensing. Check connections and battery; look for VS marks on artifact.
      Undersensing
      Spikes land on native beats. Lower the mV number. Risk: R-on-T.
      Oversensing
      Pauses, VS marks on noise. Raise the mV number; VOO briefly if dependent.
      Safety margins
      Output 2–3× capture threshold. Sensitivity about half the sensing threshold.
      Controls
      Drag knobs up/down, scroll, or use −/+. PAUSE is hold-to-pause (max 10 s). EMERGENCY = DOO 80, A 20 mA, V 25 mA.

      Educational simulation for epicardial or transvenous temporary pacing. Physiology is simplified and thresholds are scenario-set. Not a substitute for your institution's protocols or device manual.

          Step 1. What is the timing error?

            Teaching points, deep dive & references

              Event log

              • Events appear here as they happen.

              Waveform landmarks

              PSP
              Patient (unassisted) systolic pressure.
              DN / IP
              Dicrotic notch = aortic valve closure. Inflation point should sit right on it, forming a sharp V.
              PDP
              Peak diastolic (augmented) pressure. Ideally higher than PSP: this is the coronary perfusion boost.
              BAEDP
              Balloon-assisted end-diastolic pressure. Should be lower than PAEDP: the LV ejects into a partly emptied aorta.
              PAEDP
              Patient (unassisted) aortic end-diastolic pressure.
              APSP
              Assisted peak systolic pressure: the beat after an augmented beat. Should be lower than PSP.

              Educational simulation. Real consoles auto-time from the ECG or pressure trigger; this trainer uses manual offsets so you can see what each error does. Assess timing at 1:2.

                Teaching points, deep dive & references

                  Event log

                  • Events appear here as they happen.

                  Bedside reference

                  Square wave test
                  Fast flush for about a second, release, count oscillations. 1.5–2 then baseline = optimal. Fewer and slow = overdamped. 3 or more = underdamped.
                  Overdamped
                  Systolic falsely low, diastolic falsely high, MAP about right. Air bubble, clot, kink, soft tubing, low bag pressure.
                  Underdamped
                  Systolic falsely high (overshoot), diastolic low, MAP about right. Long or extra tubing, too many stopcocks.
                  Leveling
                  Transducer at the phlebostatic axis. Below the heart reads high, above reads low: about 0.74 mmHg per cm.
                  Zeroing
                  Off to patient, open to air, zero, back to patient. Re-zero per protocol and when readings don't match the cuff.

                  Educational simulation. The transducer is modelled as a second-order system (natural frequency and damping). Follow your unit's arterial line policy.

                    Teaching points, deep dive & references

                      Event log

                      • Events appear here as they happen.

                      CALS protocol

                      VF / pulseless VT
                      1. 3 stacked shocks within the first minute, no CPR in between
                      2. Then CPR, amiodarone 300 mg (or lidocaine 1 mg/kg)
                      3. Resternotomy by 5 minutes; internal shocks (commonly 20 J)
                      Asystole / severe bradycardia
                      1. Pace DDD 80–100 at maximum output (or emergency asynchronous)
                      2. CPR if no output within a minute; atropine not recommended
                      3. Resternotomy by 5 minutes
                      PEA
                      1. CPR; pause any pacing to check for hidden VF
                      2. Treat causes: tamponade, bleeding, tension pneumothorax, hypovolemia
                      3. Early resternotomy
                      Throughout
                      1. FiO2 100%, bag, remove PEEP, check tube and both lungs
                      2. No routine full-dose epinephrine or vasopressin
                      3. CPR target: systolic > 60 on the art line; if not reached, reopen
                      4. Stop pre-arrest infusions once CPR is established; IABP to pressure trigger 1:1
                      5. Six roles: compressions, airway, defib/pacing, leader, drugs, ICU coordinator

                      Educational simulation based on the STS 2017 expert consensus for resuscitation after cardiac surgery (and the related EACTS/CALS guidance). The STS document does not specify an internal defibrillation energy; 20 J is common practice. Follow your unit's arrest protocol.

                          Event log

                          • Events appear here as they happen.

                          Reading the TEG

                          R time (normal ~5–10 min)
                          Long: heparin (corrects with heparinase → protamine) or factor deficiency (stays long → FFP, or PCC for refractory coagulopathy).
                          Alpha angle / functional fibrinogen
                          Low: fibrinogen → cryo or fibrinogen concentrate.
                          MA (normal ~50–70 mm)
                          Low: platelets (count or function) and fibrinogen.
                          LY30 (normal < ~8%)
                          High: fibrinolysis → tranexamic acid.
                          Everything normal, still bleeding
                          Surgical bleeding: call the surgeon.

                          Educational simulation. TEG values and thresholds are illustrative; use your institution's transfusion algorithm.

                            Teaching points, deep dive & references

                              Event log

                              • Events appear here as they happen.

                              Quick reference

                              Impella placement signal
                              Aortic waveform = outlet in the aorta. Ventricular waveform = too deep.
                              Impella motor current
                              Pulsatile = straddling the valve (good). Flat = all in the LV or all in the aorta.
                              Suction
                              LV underfilled: hypovolemia, RV failure, tamponade, malposition. Lower P-level, fix filling.
                              VA-ECMO LV distension
                              Lost pulse pressure, rising PAWP, pulmonary edema. Lower flow, inotrope, vent.
                              Differential hypoxia
                              Right radial SpO2 low, post-oxygenator fine. Optimize vent, raise flow, consider V-AV.
                              Chatter
                              Drainage collapsing the vein: lower RPM, give volume, look for the cause.

                              Educational simulation with a simplified flow model. Device settings, alarms and numbers are illustrative; follow your ECMO/MCS team's protocols.

                                Teaching points, deep dive & references

                                  Event log

                                  • Events appear here as they happen.

                                  Post-op AF quick reference

                                  Unstable
                                  Synchronized cardioversion now (sedate if aware). Check SYNC after every shock.
                                  Stable, normal EF
                                  Beta-blocker first line for rate; diltiazem is an alternative; amiodarone for rhythm control.
                                  Reduced EF or soft BP
                                  Amiodarone; digoxin as an add-on. Avoid diltiazem; beta-blockers cautiously.
                                  Always
                                  K ≥ 4.0, Mg ≥ 2.0. Look for triggers: pain, volume, effusion, beta-blocker withdrawal.
                                  Regular 150
                                  Think flutter with 2:1 block: the atrial electrogram shows it. Overdrive pace or cardiovert.
                                  Anticoagulation
                                  When bleeding risk allows, especially if AF lasts > 48 h or recurs. Cardioversion after > 48 h needs anticoagulation or TEE first (unless unstable).

                                  Educational simulation. Drug effects and timing are simplified; check doses and contraindications against your institution's protocols.

                                        Teaching points, deep dive & references

                                          Event log

                                          • Your answers appear here.

                                          Strip-reading routine

                                          1 · Rate
                                          300 / big boxes between R waves, or count QRS in 6 s × 10.
                                          2 · Regular?
                                          Irregularly irregular = AF (or multifocal). Regularly irregular = grouped beating (Wenckebach, bigeminy).
                                          3 · P waves
                                          Present? Upright in II? One per QRS? Sawtooth? Use the A-wire EGM.
                                          4 · PR
                                          0.12–0.20 s. Lengthening = Mobitz I; fixed with drops = Mobitz II; none = dissociation.
                                          5 · QRS
                                          Narrow (< 0.12 s) = supraventricular. Wide = ventricular, aberrancy or paced.
                                          6 · Perfusion
                                          Read the arterial line: rhythm and output are separate questions.

                                          Educational strips with simplified waveforms. Use the full 12-lead and the clinical picture at the bedside.

                                          Case

                                            Teaching points, deep dive & references

                                              Event log

                                              • Events appear here as they happen.

                                              Quick reference

                                              Potassium
                                              ~10 mEq raises K ~0.1. IV: ≤ 10 mEq/h peripheral, ≤ 20 mEq/h central, never push. Fix Mg first or alongside.
                                              Hyperkalemia
                                              Stabilize (Ca), shift (insulin 10 u + 25 g dextrose, albuterol, HCO₃ if acidotic), remove (diuresis, binder, dialysis). Stop K sources.
                                              Magnesium
                                              Mg sulfate 2 g IV over 1 h; target ≥ 2.0 mg/dL with arrhythmias.
                                              Calcium
                                              Gluconate 1 g ≈ 4.65 mEq; chloride 1 g ≈ 13.6 mEq (central). Keep iCa ≥ 1.1 in massive transfusion.
                                              Glucose
                                              140–180 mg/dL on an insulin infusion; check hourly; avoid < 70.
                                              Drip math
                                              mL/h = dose (mcg/kg/min) × kg × 60 ÷ mcg/mL. Units/min: mL/h = dose × 60 ÷ units/mL.

                                              Educational simulation. Doses and responses are simplified; follow your institution's electrolyte, insulin and infusion protocols.

                                                Teaching points, deep dive & references

                                                  Event log

                                                  • Events appear here as they happen.

                                                  Quick reference

                                                  KDIGO staging
                                                  1: Cr 1.5–1.9× baseline or +0.3 in 48 h, or UO < 0.5 mL/kg/h 6–12 h. 2: Cr 2–2.9×, or UO < 0.5 ≥ 12 h. 3: Cr ≥ 3× or ≥ 4.0, KRT, or UO < 0.3 ≥ 24 h / anuria ≥ 12 h.
                                                  Oliguria checklist
                                                  Catheter → perfusion (MAP, CI, volume) → obstruction/compartment → nephrotoxins → labs (Cr, K, acid-base, urine studies).
                                                  Furosemide stress test
                                                  1 mg/kg (naive) or 1.5 mg/kg IV; ≥ 200 mL in 2 h = lower risk of progression.
                                                  KRT indications
                                                  Refractory K, acidosis, overload with hypoxemia, uremic complications, toxins.
                                                  CRRT basics
                                                  Dose 20–25 mL/kg/h delivered. Net UF low when on pressors. Citrate first-line anticoagulation if no contraindication. FF < 20–25%.

                                                  Educational simulation with simplified renal and circuit physiology. Follow your nephrology team's protocols.

                                                    Case

                                                      Teaching points, deep dive & references

                                                        Event log

                                                        • Events appear here as they happen.

                                                        Quick reference

                                                        Heparin / ACT
                                                        Weight-based (e.g. 300–400 u/kg); ACT > 480 s on bypass is reasonable per STS 2018 (> 400 s on maximal-activation devices); recheck at regular intervals. Off-pump targets are lower and vary. Protamine ~1 mg per 100 u, slowly, after separation, suckers off.
                                                        Flow
                                                        Full flow ≈ 2.2–2.4 L/min/m². MAP on bypass about 50–80. Arterial line pressure normally < 300 mmHg.
                                                        Cannulation
                                                        Aortic cannula in and out at SBP 90–100. Aortic first, then venous; venous out first, aortic last (after protamine is tolerated).
                                                        Cardioplegia
                                                        Blood cardioplegia every 15–20 min; retrograde or ostial if AI; LV vent if the heart fibrillates or distends.
                                                        Before weaning
                                                        Clamp off, de-aired, ≥ 36 °C, ventilating, rhythm/rate (pace), K < 5.5–6, Hct and ABG OK, drips ready, TEE look.
                                                        Reperfusion VF
                                                        Internal paddles 10–20 J.

                                                        Educational simulation. Steps, timings and physiology are simplified and vary by surgeon and institution; this teaches sequence and reasoning, not technique.
